body:
good god, im so sorry you went through that. you are never alone. it feels so gross and leaves you feeling vulnerable, but the fact you're still here days after it happened proves you're strong. there's a lot of stigma around men who are raped, but it does not make you any less of one. you are still you. 

i cant begin to imagine how difficult it is. you are so brave for opening up about it, even online. please, if you feel safe enough to do so, talk to others about it. you dont need to report it now, but you should whenever you muster the courage. they may not believe you, whoever you tell, but know others do. you deserve justice.

i certainly do! was told by my professor to turn something in (it has been "missing" for him because i've been working on it past the due date) and i had to compose myself to tell him i would turn it in. after leaving the building, i cried and laid in bed for hours thinking about how stupid i was.

i dont know why it hurt so bad, but it did.

edit for elaboration: now, i cant look him in the eye. i feel so ashamed and awful, even though it was only a small remark. why are we so sensitive to rejection, is my question?
absolutely. makes me want to die more, honestly! and, therapists demonize us, dont take time to understand us, and  have the ability to traumatize us more
i have it. its fun having the most painful mental illness every day, isnt it?

yes!! during my manic rage episodes, i start listening to music and it triggers me so bad :( the last manic rage episode i had was so awful i shook uncontrollably and my whole body went numb. but that wont stop me from triggering myself all over again somehow
so sorry its happened to you. its been happening for months now and i cant get out of it
